units.translation: At 693 a condition is now set that evidently refers to Ephialtes' legislation enacted shortly before: through these new laws the Areopagus had been deprived of its supreme oversight over the entire life of the state. For the corrupt ⟦1⟧ the best restoration (better than '⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧) is ⟦4⟧, since although not this compound, yet ⟦5⟧ is familiar to Aeschylus in the meanings 'to moisten, to defile' (170, ⟦6⟧), and ⟦7⟧- indeed occurs again in ⟦8⟧ (although for this Wieseler's ⟦9⟧ is worth noting); to this then belongs the punctuation after ⟦10⟧ and the replacement of ⟦11⟧' by ⟦12⟧'.

⟦1⟧ etc. was a proverb; Diogenian. III, 55 etc. (according to which likewise one should punctuate before ⟦2⟧, G. Hermann, which has also been done in the manuscripts); one compares Eur. ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧; Theogn. 961. The poet expresses himself sharply and decisively, yet at the same time cautiously; likewise in what follows, in which the admonitions from the last stasimon (517 ff.) are partly repeated verbatim, incidentally also one of the arguments that Dindorf makes against the authenticity of these verses, against which Weil recalls ⟦5⟧ = 1096f., 1275 f. = 1138 f., 1287 f. 1171f., and ⟦6⟧ = 164 f. But also the Eumenides themselves are full of repetitions, to the advantage of exegesis and criticism, and if ever, then in these principles the saying held: ⟦7⟧.
and twice to speak the good is good
but having mixed your bright house with muddy water

V. 697 ⟦1⟧ 'to advise' as ⟦2⟧; ⟦3⟧ 'to hold in honor, to cherish' of laws ⟦4⟧ (Paley). The Areopagus with its unrestricted supreme oversight over everything had previously been a power in the state to be feared, from which the people now freed themselves.
⟦1⟧: here as often concretely the object of reverence (⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧ etc.); with
⟦1⟧ = ⟦2⟧ again expresses the combination of reverence and fear, as at 690 f.

In ⟦1⟧ the ⟦2⟧ is placed irregularly. The Scythians had from ancient times the reputation of lawfulness, Frg. 203 ⟦3⟧, and already Homer N 5 f. ⟦4⟧, from which again A. Frg. 198 is drawn, who calls them ⟦5⟧ and in any case read ⟦6⟧ in Homer. On -⟦7⟧ see on ⟦8⟧. With ⟦9⟧ the ⟦10⟧ is thought of.
a defense of the land and city
eaters of mare's-milk cheese, law-abiding Scythians
of the mare-milkers, milk-drinkers, and the Abii, most righteous of men
now emphatically the actual institution, which stands here entirely appropriately.
